chunks: From Sa'd ibn Tarif who said: I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when Jamil al-Azraq came and entered upon him.

They began talking about the afflictions of the Shi'ah and their tribulations; and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: A group of people came to 'Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas and asked them some questions similar to what you have put forth. So, they came to Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) and asked him about the matter. Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah (I swear), afflictions, poverty and being killed comes more swiftly to those who love us than racing horses or a torrential stream (rushing) to its end. And if that were not the case, we would deem you as not being one of us’.

key_terms.الصَّمَرُ: The end or destination (of a stream)

ai.seo_question: Why do tribulations come quickly befall those who love the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the deep connection between the Ahl al-Bayt and their followers, asserting that tribulations, poverty, and martyrdom are swift consequences for those who truly love them. Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) uses the simile of racing horses and rushing streams to emphasize the speed and inevitability of these trials for the lovers of the Imams.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 4. It has been narrated that Sa'd ibn Tarif said: I was with Abu Ja'far (a.s) when Jamil al-Azraq came by to visit.

They began talking about the afflictions of the Shi'ah and their tribulations; and Abu Ja'far (a.s) said: A group of people came to 'Ali ibn Al-Husayn (a.s) and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas and asked them some questions similar to what you have put forth. So, they came to Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (a.s) and asked him about the matter. Al-Husayn (a.s) said: 'By Allah (I swear), afflictions, poverty and being killed comes more swiftly to those who love us than racing horses or a torrential stream (rushing) to its end. And if that were not the case, we would deem you as not being one of us’.
